findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Two aluminum cans stored in the dry storage area were observed with deep dents around the body of the can. The cans were shown to the PIC and pulled from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that aluminum cans are maintained in good condition and are never dented to prevent possibly contaminating food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A package of shredded cheese was being stored inside an unrefrigerated piece of equipment (in main service area). The equipment was once used for cold holding but is now used for bakery treats that don’t require refrigeration. Discussed and shown to PIC. The package of cheese was discarded. Be sure that temperature control foods are cold held at 41F or less to ensure proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: A buildup of black mold was observed along the back of the triple sink in the dish room. Discussed with PIC and a work order was placed to clean and re-caulk the affected area of the sink. Ensure that the back of triple sinks are maintained in good repair to prevent debris and mold buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The sanitizer bucket in the lobby area was observed to have a buildup of food debris. PIC noted that the bucket hadn’t been changed recently and that the facility was experiencing staffing issues. The bucket was taken back to be replaced with fresh water. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommendation and that the bucket is changed every few hours. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink in the bakery area is observed to not have paper towels available. The paper towel dispenser is being stocked during today’s inspection. Have each hand sink station is checked daily to ensure they are properly equipped with paper towels and all other required items.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The ceiling and portions of the walls of the walk-in freezer are observed to have an excessive accumulation of ice buildup that has made contact with a variety of food items. These food items are currently wrapped, but the amount of ice is beginning to compromise the integrity of some of the packaging. PIC stated that conversation with facility engineers is taking place on how to prevent the ice build-up, but no action plan has been set in place. Inspector spoke with PIC and established a weekly scraping of the ice build-up until the freezer can be repaired in a manner to prevent the ice accumulation. A follow-up will be taking place 12/12/2023 to observe the walk-in freezer having had the current ice build-up removed and then to discuss action plans to prevent it from accumulating again.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following pieces of equipment in the kitchen were observed to have food residue/soils on the bottom shelves that will need to be cleaned and sanitized:
-The cook-line hot box
-The cook-line double door freezer
Ensure these areas are regularly cleaned and sanitized to prevent the accumulation of food residues. Ensure all prep coolers and freezers are checked daily to ensure their cleanliness. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The dish machine is observed to be leaking water under the machine. Facility will be contacting their repair company, Hobart, to come in and perform maintenance on the machine/plumbing line in order to prevent the machine from leaking water onto the floor. Ensure equipment is regularly checked and repaired to prevent leaks form taking place from equipment.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following areas int he kitchen are observed to be in need of detailed cleaning to remove dust/soil/debris build-up:
-The air vents in the kitchen, especially by the dish area, are observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris
-Under equipment in storage rooms, especially under shelving units, has an accumulation of soil/debris.
-The electrical wires above the breakfast steam table in the kitchen are observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris.
Ensure these areas, as well as the entire kitchen, is thoroughly inspected and regularly cleaned to prevent the accumulation of dust/soil/debris on, under, and above equipment. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Employee in dish area was observed dunking hands and arms in sanitizer solution at the 3 part sink and then proceeded to the dish machine to handle clean dishes. Employee was advised on proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink between tasks and prior to handling clean dishes. Employee washed hands at the handwashing sink before handling clean dishes.
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 1) Utensils, an aerosol can, sponge, and scissors were observed in the basin of the handwashing sink adjacent to the cafeteria garbage conveyor line in the back of the dish room. Items were removed from the basin.
2) Carts were in front of the handwashing sink and blocking access in the catering/prep area. Carts were moved to allow access to the handwashing sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Ensure handwashing sinks are accessible at all times and used properly. Handwashing sinks should not be used for storage of items in the basins for any reason or as a dump/rinse sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Potholder was observed in direct contact with baked stuffing recently removed from the oven. Potholder was relocated. Employee stated potholder was temporarily put on the pans of stuffing so other people wouldn’t touch them. Use a food safe barrier and not a general surface for such purposes in the future. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket in back prep area was observed with concentration below 100ppm quat. Solution was said to be made within the half hour prior. Fresh solution was provided and observed at 400ppm. Staff were advised to let the dispenser run for several seconds prior to filling buckets to allow product to properly suction through the line when preparing quat solutions. Use test strips to verify concnetation is maintained at 200-400ppm as required per manufacturer’s instructions. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Potatoes in steam table at kitchen service line had surface and internal temperatures at 113F-118F. Potatoes were discarded and fresh product was provided. Holding well was observed with an open space where a pan was removed and product was no longer needed. Best practices for storage to help maintain heat were discussed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 An active fruit fly population was observed in the dish room, with the most activity noted around the garbage disposal at the 3 part sink and under the cafeteria garbage conveyor belt. Flies were also clustered around a soiled dust pan by the mopsink and in a floor drain beneath the cafeteria garbage conveyor belt. General cleaning and repairs to help aid in fly management were discussed. Management already requested additional service with their pest control company, and PCO is currently scheduled to come in once a week at this time for service. Re-inspection will be conducted in ~2hrs to check on the status of pest control.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Drain line to ice machine bin was slightly askew and draining on the floor underneath. Adjust the drain line to allow for proper drainage in the floor drain. 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law. Route waste to public sewer system per Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed roast beef to be documented as being probed at 49F at 2:30 on the cold sandwich bar log sheet. The same roast beef was placed underneath the ice baths with fresh product in it on the bar. It was discussed that since the roast beef was probed out of temperature (which inspector confirmed by probing the roast beef as well), and the last documented temperature was taken at 10:30 am, roast beef should have been discarded rather than placed under the fresh product to cool since it is unknown how long it had been out of temperature. Alternatively, since product was maintained at <70F, it could have been served for 2 additional hours before being discarded. Roast beef was discarded during the inspection. Make sure employees know the corrective action when a product is out of temperature.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

Observed the sprayer nozzle at the three compartment sink to be hanging below the flood rim of the sink and in contact with soiled water. Provide sprayer nozzle to be at least 2" above flood rim.
750-1080 The potable water system shall be installed to preclude the possibility of backflow.  Devices to protect against backflow and back siphonage shall be installed at all fixtures and equipment where an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water inlet is not provided between the water outlet from the fixture and the fixture’s flood-level rim and wherever else backflow or backsiphonage may occur. Install backflow prevention device.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice cream freezer in the self serve area to have some ice accumulation.  Defrost the freezer.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed the lids in the soda area to be stored improperly.  Properly store the single service lids to avoid from contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the handsink in the dish room to have an absence caulk. 2) Observed the handsink in the bakery area to have an absence of caulk. Re-caulk the sinks.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: CORRECTED > Observed moist wiping cloth to be stored on the assembly line counter next to the room service cooler. Cloth was placed into proper concentration sanitizer solution for storage. 750-810 Moist cloths for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be clean and rinsed frequently and stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) The tops of coolers and freezer and other equipment with heavier accumulation on paper towel dispenser in the bakery. 2) The ledge above the three compartment sink in the dish area with debris and lime scale. 3) The bottoms of the movable dry storage racks in the dry storage area with debris. 4) The exterior of the hand sink at the grill service line. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors to be soiled in the following areas: 1) Under the soda rack next to the dry storage area with food splash. 2) In the walk-in freezer under shelving units with food debris. 3) Under the drink station cabinets in the self-service area with debris accumulation. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: CORRECTED > Observed a bottle labeled as sanitizer to contain a general cleaner next to the three compartment sink outside the walk-in coolers. Bottle was discarded by employee. 750-1300 Properly label poisonous or toxic materials.
